4.grammar: A proper name (of foreign, non-Arabic origin). Names of this kind are diptotes: they do not take case-tanwīn, and their accusative and genitive both show a single -a ending. The -a here marks the word as an object or as the noun governed by a preposition rather than carrying full case inflection.

5.meaning: And he/it was terrified, startled, or thrown into alarm — the verb fazi'a denotes the sudden onset of fear or fright, the jolt of terror.

parts.en: he was terrified, he was alarmed (past tense verb)

5.grammar: The conjunction fa- ('and so'/'then', marking a consequence or sequence) prefixed to the Form I verb fazi'a in the perfect (past) tense, 3rd person masculine singular. The -a ending marks the past tense 3rd person masculine singular. The verb describes the experience of being seized by sudden, alarming fear.
5.root: ف-ز-ع (f-z-') — to be frightened, to be startled, to be alarmed

6.meaning: From them / among them — the preposition min ('from, out of, part of') joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
6.grammar: The preposition min ('from / among / part of') with the attached third-person masculine plural pronoun -hum ('them'). Pronouns after a preposition are in the genitive; the combination expresses origin, partition ('some of them'), or belonging to that group.
6.root: — (preposition with pronoun, no root)

7.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.
7.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, utterance

8.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
8.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

9.meaning: Do not fear; do not be afraid. A command form telling someone to refrain from fear.
9.grammar: A second-person masculine singular verb ('you') in the jussive mood, shown by the cut-off final consonant with no extra vowel. This clipped form is what follows a negative command particle, giving the sense 'do not fear'.

10.meaning: 'Two adversaries / two opposing parties' — a matched pair of disputants set against each other in a quarrel or legal contest. The dual ending shows there are exactly two opposing sides.
10.grammar: A masculine noun in the dual ('exactly two'). The ending -āni is the dual in its nominative (subject) form: it marks a pair and indicates they function as the subject or as a simple predicate ('they two are …').
10.root: خ-ص-م (kh-ṣ-m) — to dispute, quarrel, litigate; adversary, opposing party

11.meaning: 'He overstepped / wronged / acted oppressively' — to transgress the bounds of fairness, to encroach on another's right and behave unjustly. The base sense is of exceeding proper limits and seeking what is not one's due.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he did it'). The final long -ā stands in place of a weak final root letter; with no added subject suffix, the bare form denotes a completed act by a single male ('he transgressed').
11.root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y) — to seek/desire; to exceed bounds, transgress, oppress

12.meaning: A noun-plus-pronoun meaning 'some of us' or 'a part of us' — baʿḍ denotes a portion, part, or some members of a larger whole, here joined to 'us'.
12.grammar: A noun ('a part, some') with the attached pronoun -nā ('us/our') making it 'some of us'. The -u ending on the noun is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject or doer of a sentence (the one performing the action).

13.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
13.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

14.meaning: 'Some (others)' / 'a part' — the same noun for 'a portion or some,' here left indefinite, often functioning as the counterpart in the 'one another' construction.
14.grammar: A noun 'part/some' in the genitive case with indefinite marking (the -in ending, called tanwīn). The genitive typically follows a preposition or links it to a preceding noun ('… of …'); the doubled -n sound marks it as indefinite ('a part / some').
14.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, or some of a whole

15.meaning: A command meaning 'so judge / then decide / then rule,' addressed to one person. It calls for rendering a verdict or governing decision. The leading particle adds 'so/then,' tying the command to what precedes as its consequence.
15.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a second-person masculine singular 'you.' The 'fa-' prefix means 'so/then,' marking the order as a result of what came before. The stem carries a written helping vowel at its start; the verb ends in a silent consonant (sukūn), which is the normal form of a singular command.

16.meaning: 'Between us' — the spatial or relational word for 'between/among', with 'us' attached: the space, relation, or matter standing between ourselves.
16.grammar: An adverb of place 'between', fixed in the -a form, with the attached pronoun -na ('us'). Together they mean 'between us / among us', marking a relation linking two or more parties.
16.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

17.meaning: 'With the truth / by means of what is true and right.' Combines the preposition 'with/by' and 'the truth' — that which is real, established, correct, and rightfully due, as opposed to falsehood.
17.grammar: A noun governed by the attached preposition bi- ('with/by'). The -i ending is the genitive case, which is required after a preposition; here it links 'the truth' to 'with', giving 'with the truth'.
17.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, reality, that which is established and due

18.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
18.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

19.meaning: '(Do not) act unjustly / go to excess' — to deviate from fairness, to be wrongful and overbearing in judgement. The verb conveys swerving away from what is right and equitable.
19.grammar: A second-person masculine singular verb in the jussive (the form taken after a negative/prohibitive particle, 'do not …') of the doubled root ش-ط-ط. This is Form I: in the jussive the normally-doubled final letter splits apart (تُشِطُّ becomes تُشۡطِطۡ), so the two identical letters are written out and the final one takes a silent sukūn. The tu- prefix marks 'you (one man)' as the doer.
19.root: ش-ط-ط (sh-ṭ-ṭ) — to be far/remote, exceed bounds; injustice, excess

20.meaning: 'And guide us' — a plea to be led to the right way, shown the correct path, and directed toward what is true and good. The verb is a request, asking the one addressed to provide guidance to the speaker's group.

parts.en: helping vowel to begin the word

20.grammar: An imperative ('guide!') addressed to a single male, with the object pronoun -nā ('us') attached and prefixed by wa- ('and'). It begins with a helping alif (an 'i' sound) to ease pronunciation; its final root vowel is dropped (the jussive shape proper to a command), and -nā marks the speaker's group as the one being guided.
20.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead aright, show the way

21.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
21.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

22.meaning: 'Fair / equitable / common' — even-handed and just; something equal, level, or held in common between parties.
22.grammar: An indefinite noun/adjective meaning 'equity, fairness, an even thing'. The -in ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite and in the genitive case — used after a preposition or to describe a preceding genitive noun ('a word that is fair'). It conveys evenness and impartiality.

23.meaning: The path, the road, the way — especially a clear, broad highway; used figuratively for the way of life or course one travels.
23.grammar: A masculine noun with the definite article 'the'. The final -i is the genitive case ending, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the path') or follows a preposition. (The 'l' of the article assimilates in sound to the following ṣ, hence 'aṣ-ṣirāṭ'.)

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
2.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

3.meaning: The noun 'brother' joined to 'my' — a male sibling, and more broadly a close kinsman or fellow. The form expresses 'my brother.'
3.grammar: The base noun is akh ('brother'). The attached long -ī is the first-person possessive pronoun 'my.' This possessive ending absorbs the case-vowel, so the word reads simply 'my brother' regardless of its grammatical position.
3.root: ا-خ-و (ʾ-kh-w) — brotherhood, kinship, being a sibling

4.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
4.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

5.meaning: The number nine (in the feminine form used with masculine-counted nouns). A cardinal number naming the count nine.
5.grammar: A cardinal number 'nine' with nunation. The final -un is the nominative case with nunation: the nominative marks a subject or simple predicate, and the added 'n' sound marks it as indefinite. (In Arabic counting, this feminine-shaped 'nine' is the form used when the things counted are grammatically masculine.)
5.root: ت-س-ع (t-s-ʿ) — the number nine

6.meaning: 'And ninety' — the round number ninety. Joined by 'and' to a preceding unit, it combines to express a compound number in the nineties.
6.grammar: A 'tens' number ('ninety') prefixed with wa- ('and'). It takes the sound-masculine-plural ending; the -ūna form here is the nominative (subject) shape, used for a subject or simple predicate. The 'tens' from twenty to ninety all share this -ūna / -īna pattern.
6.root: ت-س-ع (t-s-ʿ) — the number nine (hence ninety)

7.meaning: A ewe — a female sheep. The word names a single adult female of the flock.
7.grammar: A feminine singular noun (marked by the tā' marbūṭa, the rounded final 't') with nunation. The final -tan is the accusative case with nunation: the accusative typically marks an object of a verb or a noun specifying a number, and the added 'n' sound marks it as indefinite ('a ewe').
7.root: ن-ع-ج (n-ʿ-j) — ewe, female sheep (the root denotes whiteness/the sheep)

8.meaning: 'and for me / and to me there is…': expresses that something belongs to, or is available to, the speaker. The opening 'and' joins it to what precedes.
8.grammar: A small phrase: wa- ('and') + the preposition li- ('for/to', indicating possession or benefit) + the pronoun 'me'. With the attached 'me', the preposition takes the form li-ya. It conveys 'and for me there is/are…', stating that something pertains to the speaker.

9.meaning: A ewe — a female sheep. The word names a single adult female of the flock.
9.grammar: A feminine singular noun (marked by the tā' marbūṭa, the rounded final 't') with nunation. The final -un is the nominative case with nunation: the nominative marks a subject or simple predicate, and the added 'n' sound marks it as indefinite ('a ewe').
9.root: ن-ع-ج (n-ʿ-j) — ewe, female sheep (the root denotes whiteness/the sheep)

10.meaning: Single / one — a feminine adjective affirming that the blast is only one, emphasising its unitary and decisive nature.
10.grammar: Wāḥida is the feminine form of wāḥid. The -atun ending (tanwīn ḍamma on tāʾ marbūṭa) marks the nominative indefinite, agreeing with the feminine zajra as its adjective or appositive.
10.root: و-ح-د (w-ḥ-d) — to be one, unique, alone

11.meaning: 'Then he said / so he said' — the past-tense verb 'he said,' introduced by a connector meaning 'then / so,' marking what follows as the next or resulting step.
11.grammar: The prefix fa- means 'then / so,' linking this to what came before and often implying sequence or consequence. The verb is past-tense, third-person masculine singular ('he'); the final -a is the base vowel of the 3rd-person masculine singular past form, marking that a single masculine subject performed the action.

12.meaning: 'Hand her over to me / put her in my charge' — a demand that something be made over to the speaker's keeping and responsibility, transferred into his care. The base verb is about taking charge of, sponsoring, or guaranteeing something.
12.grammar: A causative (form IV) imperative addressed to a single male, carrying two attached object pronouns: -nī ('me', the recipient) and -hā ('her', the thing handed over). The opening a- is the command-vowel of this verb pattern; the verb means 'cause (me) to take charge (of her)'.
12.root: ك-ف-ل (k-f-l) — to take charge of, sponsor, guarantee, give into one's keeping

13.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'he overpowered me / he prevailed over me by force,' carrying the sense of overbearing strength — to be mightier than someone and dominate them in argument or contention.
13.grammar: A third-person masculine singular past-tense verb ('he did'), with the attached -nī meaning 'me' as its object. The doubled middle consonant (ʿazz-) is the intensive pattern, conveying overpowering strength. The -a ending on the verb stem marks the standard masculine 'he' past form.

14.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
14.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

15.meaning: Address, discourse, the act of speaking to someone — formal speech directed at an audience, and by extension the give-and-take of conversation or a settled manner of expression.
15.grammar: A definite verbal noun (al- = 'the'). Its bare final -i (no nunation, since al- makes it definite) is the genitive case — the case a noun takes after a preposition or when joined to a preceding noun ('… of …').
15.root: خ-ط-ب (kh-ṭ-b) — to address, speak to; speech, discourse, a weighty matter

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

2.meaning: A two-part emphasis particle meaning 'surely, indeed (already)' — 'la-' strongly affirms, and 'qad' before a past verb stresses that the action has definitely occurred.
2.grammar: Two particles fused for emphasis. 'la-' is the affirming prefix 'surely / truly.' 'qad,' when it precedes a past-tense verb, confirms and intensifies that the action really happened ('has indeed …'). Together they give a strong oath-like assurance to the statement that follows.

3.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'he wronged you / treated you unjustly,' from a root whose core sense is putting something out of its rightful place — to oppress, to deal unfairly, to transgress against another's due.
3.grammar: A third-person masculine singular past-tense verb ('he did'), with the attached -ka meaning 'you' (a single male) as its object. The -a after the stem is the standard 'he' past-tense marker.
3.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — wrong, injustice, oppression (placing a thing where it does not belong)

4.meaning: A noun phrase meaning 'by the asking for / by the demanding of,' i.e., a request or petition to be given something — governed by the preposition 'with/by.'
4.grammar: A noun preceded by the preposition bi- ('by/with'). The -i ending is genitive: prepositions like bi- always pull the following noun into this case, and it also links the noun to a following noun ('the asking OF …').

5.meaning: A noun meaning 'a ewe' (a female sheep), with an attached pronoun making it 'your ewe.'
5.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the attached possessive -ka ('your,' addressing one male). The noun's feminine ending tā' marbūṭa (ة) opens to a full -t- (giving naʿjat-) whenever a suffix is attached to it. The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case marker, which appears because a possessive pronoun is attached, signalling the relationship 'the ewe OF you.'
5.root: ن-ع-ج (n-ʿ-j) — ewe, female sheep

6.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
6.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

7.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'ewes' (female sheep), with an attached pronoun making it 'his ewes.'
7.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun with the attached possessive -hi ('his'). The -i ending is genitive, here triggered by the attached possessive pronoun, marking 'the ewes OF him.' The pronoun takes the -hi form (with 'i') because it follows a genitive vowel.
7.root: ن-ع-ج (n-ʿ-j) — ewe, female sheep

8.meaning: 'And indeed' / 'and truly' — the joining word 'wa' ('and') attached to the emphatic particle 'inna', which introduces a statement and strongly affirms it, adding certainty like 'surely' or 'indeed'.
8.grammar: A connective 'wa' ('and') plus 'inna', a particle of emphasis that opens a nominal sentence. 'Inna' puts its following noun (the subject) into the accusative case while strongly affirming the truth of the statement.

9.meaning: An adjective/noun meaning 'many', 'much', or 'numerous' — a large quantity or great number of something.
9.grammar: Adjective/noun in the indefinite accusative, marked by the final -an (the 'tanwīn' of fatḥa). The accusative case here commonly marks an object of a verb or an indefinite quantity; the doubled-n sound (nunation) signals that the word is indefinite ('many', not 'the many').
9.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be much, many, abundant

10.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
10.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

11.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'the associates / the partners / those mixed together,' referring to people whose affairs or properties are intermingled, such as business partners or co-owners who share intermingled holdings.
11.grammar: A plural noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending is genitive: it typically marks the noun as object of a preposition or as linked to a following noun ('… OF …'). The pattern fuʿalāʾ here describes a class of people sharing a quality (intermingling).

12.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he/it surely transgresses / oppresses / acts wrongfully against,' from a root meaning to exceed proper bounds, to seek what is not one's right, to behave with hostility.
12.grammar: A third-person masculine singular present-tense verb ('he does / is doing'), prefixed with emphatic la- ('surely, certainly'). The ya- prefix marks the 'he' subject; the verb ends in long -ī because its final root letter is a weak/defective letter (yā'), giving the verb a -ī ending in this form.
12.root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y) — to seek wrongfully, transgress, exceed bounds, oppress

13.meaning: 'Some of them' / 'a part of them' — a noun meaning 'a portion, part, or some' joined to an attached pronoun 'them'. Often paired with itself to express 'one another / each other'.
13.grammar: A noun 'part/some' in the nominative case (the -u ending), which typically marks it as the subject or doer. The suffix -hum is a genitive (possessive) pronoun meaning 'their' (masculine plural); attached to a noun this way it sits in the possessor slot, giving 'some of them'.
13.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, or some of a whole

14.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
14.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

15.meaning: 'Some (others)' / 'a part' — the same noun for 'a portion or some,' here left indefinite, often functioning as the counterpart in the 'one another' construction.
15.grammar: A noun 'part/some' in the genitive case with indefinite marking (the -in ending, called tanwīn). The genitive typically follows a preposition or links it to a preceding noun ('… of …'); the doubled -n sound marks it as indefinite ('a part / some').
15.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, or some of a whole

16.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
16.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

17.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
17.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

18.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
18.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

19.meaning: A two-part word: 'and' + 'they did / worked / performed.' The verb denotes doing deeds, working, putting effort into action — practical doing as opposed to mere speaking or believing.
19.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' + a past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural. The -ū ending marks the subject as 'they' (a group of males or a mixed group): 'and they did / worked.'

20.meaning: 'The righteous deeds / good works' — the definite plural of a word meaning that which is sound, wholesome, upright, and beneficial. As a noun it refers to good, virtuous actions that set things right.
20.grammar: A definite sound feminine plural noun ('the good deeds'). The -i ending is the oblique case used by feminine plurals to mark either the genitive ('… of …' / after a preposition) or the accusative (direct object); for this plural pattern the accusative and genitive share the same -i ending.
20.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound, good, upright, set right

21.meaning: And a few / a small number / little — an adjective-noun meaning small in quantity. It can describe people who are few or an amount that is slight.
21.grammar: Connector wa- ('and') plus an adjective/noun meaning 'few, little', indefinite, in the nominative (the -un ending). Nominative typically marks the subject or the thing being affirmed ('and a few [are] …'). It conveys smallness of number or amount.
21.root: ق-ل-ل (q-l-l) — to be few, little, scant

22.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
22.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

23.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
23.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

24.meaning: 'And he/it supposed, thought, assumed, was convinced' — a past-tense verb of opinion or conjecture, ranging from strong supposition to firm belief depending on context.
24.grammar: Past tense (completed action), third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The doubled final n reflects the root's geminate form. The prefixed wa- means 'and'.

25.meaning: The proper name Dāwūd (the Prophet and King David), to whom the Psalms (Zabūr) were revealed.
25.grammar: A proper name. The final '-u' is the nominative ending, the case that typically marks the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. As a diptote name it takes a bare '-u' without nunation (no final '-n' sound).

26.meaning: A compound particle meaning 'that …' or 'only that' — it introduces and emphasizes a fact as the content of a thought or statement; 'anna' asserts ('indeed/that') and the attached 'mā' often gives a restrictive sense ('that … is only …').
26.grammar: A combination of the emphatic particle 'anna' ('that, indeed') with 'mā'. 'Anna' introduces a noun-clause as the object of verbs like 'think' or 'know', putting the following noun in the accusative. Joined with 'mā' it frequently carries a limiting force, 'only/merely'. Particles like this do not themselves take case endings.

27.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'We tested him / tried him,' from a root whose core sense is testing or trial — putting through hardship or temptation to prove or refine, originally the smelting of gold to separate it from dross.
27.grammar: A past-tense verb with the suffix -nā meaning 'we' as the subject (the doubled 'n' shows the stem's final 'n' meeting the 'n' of 'we'), and the attached -hu meaning 'him' as its object. The -ā vowel carries the 'we did' meaning.
27.root: ف-ت-ن (f-t-n) — trial, testing, temptation (refining gold by fire)

28.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'so he sought forgiveness / asked for pardon,' i.e., he asked his Lord to cover over and pardon his sins.
28.grammar: A third-person masculine singular past-tense verb ('he did'), preceded by fa- ('so/then'). The ista- pattern conveys actively seeking or requesting something — here 'to seek forgiveness.' The -a ending marks the standard masculine 'he' past form.
28.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to forgive, cover over, pardon

29.meaning: The noun 'Lord' joined to a 'his' pronoun — 'his Lord'. Rabb conveys the Master and Sustainer who owns, nurtures, and brings a thing to its full development; far richer than 'lord' alone.
29.grammar: A noun with the attached possessive pronoun -hu ('his'). The -a ending is accusative, the case used when the noun is an object of a verb or otherwise governed into that case; -hu means it belongs to 'him'.
29.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, ownership, nurturing and sustaining to completion

30.meaning: 'And he/it fell down' — 'and' joined to a verb meaning to collapse, tumble, or drop heavily to the ground.
30.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') joined to a past-tense verb for a single masculine subject ('he/it fell'). The doubled 'r' (shadda) is part of the root, conveying a sudden, heavy falling or collapsing down.
30.root: خ-ر-ر (kh-r-r) — to fall down, collapse, tumble

31.meaning: An active participle meaning 'bowing / one who bows down,' describing someone in the posture of humble bending, especially the bowing of worship and submission before Allah.
31.grammar: An active participle ('one who bows') functioning as a descriptive noun. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative: it commonly marks a word describing the manner or state in which an action is done ('… while bowing') or serves as an object.
31.root: ر-ك-ع (r-k-ʿ) — to bow, bend the body low (in reverence)

32.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'and he turned back / returned in repentance,' carrying the sense of turning penitently to Allah and returning to Him again and again.
32.grammar: A third-person masculine singular past-tense verb ('he did'), preceded by wa- ('and'). The pattern (a- prefix with a long internal -ā-) gives a sense of turning toward / directing oneself back. The -a final vowel marks the standard masculine 'he' past form.
32.root: ن-و-ب (n-w-b) — to turn back, return repeatedly, turn penitently

1.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'so We forgave / pardoned,' i.e., covered over and remitted the fault.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb preceded by fa- ('so/then'), with the suffix -nā meaning 'we' as the subject. The -nā ending tells you the doers are 'we'; the action is completed (past tense).
1.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to forgive, cover over, pardon

2.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
2.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

3.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
3.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

4.meaning: 'And indeed' / 'and truly' — the joining word 'wa' ('and') attached to the emphatic particle 'inna', which introduces a statement and strongly affirms it, adding certainty like 'surely' or 'indeed'.
4.grammar: A connective 'wa' ('and') plus 'inna', a particle of emphasis that opens a nominal sentence. 'Inna' puts its following noun (the subject) into the accusative case while strongly affirming the truth of the statement.

5.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
5.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

6.meaning: In our presence, with us, in our keeping or estimation — 'ʿinda' denotes nearness, possession, or being in someone's sight/judgment.

parts.en: with / at / in the presence of (locational particle)

6.grammar: An adverb of place/relation, ʿinda ('with, in the presence of'), here joined to the pronoun -nā ('us/our'). It commonly conveys possession, nearness, or 'in the view/judgment of.' The attached -nā is the first-person plural pronoun.
6.root: ع-ن-د (ʿ-n-d) — nearness, presence, being beside

7.meaning: A noun meaning 'nearness / a position of closeness,' especially nearness in rank and honor — being brought near to Allah. Prefixed with emphatic 'surely.'
7.grammar: A feminine noun ending in the fixed long -ā (alif maqṣūra), prefixed with emphatic la- ('surely, indeed'). This -ā is part of the word's fixed form and does not change for case; it is characteristic of a class of abstract feminine nouns.
7.root: ز-ل-ف (z-l-f) — to draw near, nearness, proximity (in rank)

8.meaning: And goodness/beauty (of) — the fine, excellent, or beautiful quality of a thing. 'Ḥusn' is goodness, fairness, and excellence.
8.grammar: A noun ('goodness') with the -a ending marking the accusative case — typically the direct object of a verb. Its bare (un-nunated) form signals that it is joined to a following noun in a possessive link ('the goodness of …'). The leading wa- means 'and'.

9.meaning: A place or point of return; the destination to which one ultimately comes back, and by extension one's final resort or homecoming.
9.grammar: A noun of place built on the ma- pattern, denoting where an action happens — here 'place of return.' The ending -in is genitive with nunation (the -n sound marking an indefinite noun, 'a place of return'); the genitive is the case taken after another noun or a preposition.
9.root: أ-و-ب (ʾ-w-b) — returning, coming back, turning back

1.meaning: A call meaning 'O Dāwūd (David)' — the proper name of the prophet-king David, addressed directly.
1.grammar: A vocative (direct address) built from yā ('O') plus the proper name. The -u ending is the nominative form that a directly-addressed singular name takes when called. Being a proper name, it does not take indefinite endings.

2.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
2.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

3.meaning: We made you / We appointed you / We rendered you (such-and-such). From a root meaning to make, set, place, or designate; with an attached 'you,' it conveys 'We caused you to be' or 'We assigned you.'
3.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb. The suffix -nā marks the doer as 'we'; the further suffix -ka is the object 'you (one male).' Past tense presents the making/appointing as already done.
3.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, set, place, render, appoint

4.meaning: 'A successor / vicegerent / deputy' — one who comes after and takes the place of another, succeeding to authority or responsibility; a steward who stands in for and represents the one who appointed him.
4.grammar: A noun of the 'faʿīl' pattern denoting one who succeeds or stands in for another. The final -an is the accusative case with 'tanwīn' (nunation) and indefiniteness — the accusative is the form a noun takes as the direct object of a verb (the thing being made or appointed), and the doubled-n sound marks it indefinite ('a successor'). The tā' marbūṭa (-a(t)) is a lexically inherent part of the word khalīfa, not an added suffix.
4.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — coming after, succeeding, taking another's place

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
5.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
5.root: — (particle)

6.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
6.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').
6.root: أ-ر-ض (ʾ-r-ḍ) — earth, land, ground

7.meaning: A command meaning 'so judge / then decide / then rule,' addressed to one person. It calls for rendering a verdict or governing decision. The leading particle adds 'so/then,' tying the command to what precedes as its consequence.
7.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a second-person masculine singular 'you.' The 'fa-' prefix means 'so/then,' marking the order as a result of what came before. The stem carries a written helping vowel at its start; the verb ends in a silent consonant (sukūn), which is the normal form of a singular command.
7.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — judging, ruling, wisdom

8.meaning: Between; in the midst of two things. An adverb of place marking the space separating or lying among parties or points.
8.grammar: An adverb of place ('between'). It always ends in -a and grammatically governs what follows it, putting the following noun(s) into the genitive 'of' relationship. It does not change to show 'the' or a case of its own; the fixed -a is simply how this word is formed.
8.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

9.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
9.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
9.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

10.meaning: 'With the truth / by means of what is true and right.' Combines the preposition 'with/by' and 'the truth' — that which is real, established, correct, and rightfully due, as opposed to falsehood.
10.grammar: A noun governed by the attached preposition bi- ('with/by'). The -i ending is the genitive case, which is required after a preposition; here it links 'the truth' to 'with', giving 'with the truth'.
10.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, reality, that which is established and due

11.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
11.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

12.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'you follow / pursue / go after,' from a root meaning to come behind and follow a thing's track. The doubled middle conveys earnest, persistent following.
12.grammar: A second-person masculine singular present-tense verb ('you do'). The ta- prefix marks the 'you' subject. The normal ending has been clipped (jussive mood, after a particle like 'do not'), and the final consonant takes a helping -i vowel for ease of pronunciation before a following word; this signals a command or prohibition rather than a plain statement.
12.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, come after, pursue a track

13.meaning: A noun meaning 'desire / craving / the inclination of the lower self,' i.e., whim or passion that pulls a person toward what they want rather than what is right; often it carries the negative sense of caprice opposed to guidance.
13.grammar: A masculine noun with the definite article al- ('the'), ending in the fixed long -ā (alif maqṣūra). This -ā is part of the word's fixed shape and stays the same across cases — typical of certain nouns derived from weak-lettered roots.
13.root: ه-و-ي (h-w-y) — to incline, fall toward, desire (the pull of inclination)

14.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'so it leads you astray / causes you to lose the way,' i.e., makes someone stray from the right path. Built on the causative pattern: to make another go astray.
14.grammar: A third-person masculine singular present-tense verb ('he/it does') on the causative pattern ('to make … go astray'), with attached -ka ('you') as object, preceded by fa- ('so'). The yu- prefix marks 'he/it' on this causative form. The -a ending is subjunctive, the mood that typically follows particles meaning 'so that' or expresses a resulting consequence.
14.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, lose the way, go astray

15.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

15.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

16.meaning: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
16.grammar: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.

17.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
17.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

18.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
18.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

19.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
19.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

20.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'they go astray / they stray from the path,' losing the right way or wandering in error.
20.grammar: A third-person masculine plural present-tense verb. The ya- prefix plus the -ūna ending together mean 'they (males) do / are doing.' The -ūna ending also marks the indicative mood — a plain factual statement, not a command or 'so that' clause.
20.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, lose the way, go astray

21.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

21.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

22.meaning: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
22.grammar: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.

23.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
23.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

24.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
24.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

25.meaning: Painful punishment, torment, or chastisement — suffering imposed as a penalty.
25.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject or for the thing said to exist.

26.meaning: Severe, intense, harsh, or mighty — describing something powerful and unsparing in its degree.
26.grammar: An adjective on the intensive pattern faʿīl ('severe, intense'). The final -u is the nominative ending, which generally marks the word as a subject or predicate.
26.root: ش-د-د (sh-d-d) — to be strong, intense, severe

27.meaning: A compound meaning roughly 'because of what...', 'on account of that which...', or 'by means of what...'. It joins the preposition 'with/by/because of' to a connector 'what/that which', introducing the reason or instrument for something.
27.grammar: A preposition (bi-) fused to the word mā ('what / that which'). The preposition bi- expresses cause, means, or accompaniment; combined with mā it forms a phrase pointing to the thing or fact that serves as a reason or means ('because of what...').

28.meaning: A verb meaning 'they forgot' or 'they neglected/abandoned.' The root spans both genuine forgetfulness and the willful neglect of something one chooses to put out of mind.
28.grammar: A past-tense verb. The ending -ū marks a completed action by 'they' (masculine plural). The silent 'alif' written after the -ū is a spelling convention and is not pronounced.

29.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
29.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
29.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

30.meaning: The reckoning, accounting, or calling to account — the tallying and settling of deeds; also calculation or counting in a general sense.
30.grammar: A definite verbal noun with the article 'al-' ('the'). The final -i (kasra) marks the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or as the second part of a possessive pair ('… of the reckoning').

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: We created / We brought into being — the act of originating and forming something. The verb denotes Allah's making and shaping of creation, completed in the past, with 'We' as the majestic subject.

parts.en: we (subject suffix on a past verb)

2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb describing a completed action. The suffix -nā attached to a past verb marks the subject as 'we' (used of Allah in the majestic plural). There is no separate ending beyond this pronoun, since the perfect tense fuses subject and action.
2.root: خ-ل-ق (kh-l-q) — to create, originate, shape, and proportion

3.meaning: The sky or heaven — all that rises and spreads overhead: the visible canopy above and the heights beyond it. A definite noun with the article 'al-', so 'the sky / the heaven'.
3.grammar: A definite noun (with 'al-', here assimilated to 'as-samāʾ'). The final '-a' ending is accusative: it typically marks the word as the object of a verb — the thing an action is done to — or the item being mentioned after certain particles.
3.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — to be high, lofty; that which is elevated overhead

4.meaning: 'and the earth' — the ground, land, or the planet earth; the world we stand upon, often paired with the heavens to mean all of creation.
4.grammar: A feminine noun, prefixed with 'and' and 'the.' The -a ending is accusative, the case typically marking the object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or a noun governed by certain particles.

5.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
5.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
5.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

6.meaning: Between the two of them — the space or relation lying amid a pair.
6.grammar: An adverb of place, 'between,' fixed in the accusative as adverbs of place commonly are; the -a marks its adverbial function ('in the place that is between'). The attached -humā is the dual pronoun 'the two of them' (exactly two).
6.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction; that which lies between

7.meaning: 'In vain, falsely, without purpose' — that which is futile, baseless, or empty of truth; the opposite of what is true and well-founded.
7.grammar: An active participle/noun meaning 'something false or futile.' The -an ending is accusative and indefinite, here typically describing the manner or purpose of an action ('in vain, for nothing'). It answers 'how?' or 'to what end?'
7.root: ب-ط-ل (b-ṭ-l) — to be false, vain, void, futile

8.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
8.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

9.meaning: An assumption, conjecture, or supposition — an opinion or belief held without certainty. It spans a range from mere guesswork and doubt to a strong, settled presumption, depending on context.
9.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified ('the assumption is …').

10.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
10.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

11.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
11.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

12.meaning: 'So woe …' — a connective 'so/then' plus 'woe': an exclamation of impending doom, ruin, or grievous distress called down upon someone. It is a cry of warning and lament, not a literal noun of place.
12.grammar: The connective fa- ('so / then') prefixed to the noun 'woe.' The noun stands in the nominative with indefinite marking (the -un ending, tanwīn). Used this way it functions as an exclamation — 'woe (be) to …' — typically followed by 'to/for' someone.
12.root: و-ي-ل (w-y-l) — woe; ruin, doom, grievous distress

13.meaning: 'For/to those who …' — a preposition 'for / to / belonging to' joined to the masculine plural relative pronoun 'those who,' which introduces a description of a group by something they do.
13.grammar: The preposition li- ('for / to / belonging to') fused with the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'). Relative pronouns like this do not change for case; they point ahead to a clause that describes the group ('those who …').

14.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
14.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
14.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

15.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
15.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

16.meaning: 'The Fire' — fire, flame; in religious usage often the Fire of Hell, the blazing punishment of the Hereafter.
16.grammar: The definite article 'al-' ('the') plus the feminine noun 'nār' ('fire'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (so it is pronounced 'an-nār'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the Fire').

1.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'or', specifically the 'or' that pairs with a preceding question to offer an alternative ('…or…?'). It links two possibilities being weighed against each other, often after an opening interrogative.

parts.en: or (in alternatives, esp. after a question)

1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case or tense ending). It typically introduces the second branch of a two-part question or a balanced alternative, presenting the two as equally consequential.

2.meaning: we appoint / we assign / we make — to set, render, or designate something as a particular thing or for a particular purpose.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb. The na- prefix means 'we' (the doer), and the final -u marks the ordinary (indicative) present tense: a simple statement of doing, 'we make/appoint'.
2.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, place, render, appoint

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
4.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

5.meaning: A two-part word: 'and' + 'they did / worked / performed.' The verb denotes doing deeds, working, putting effort into action — practical doing as opposed to mere speaking or believing.
5.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' + a past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural. The -ū ending marks the subject as 'they' (a group of males or a mixed group): 'and they did / worked.'
5.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act

6.meaning: 'The righteous deeds / good works' — the definite plural of a word meaning that which is sound, wholesome, upright, and beneficial. As a noun it refers to good, virtuous actions that set things right.
6.grammar: A definite sound feminine plural noun ('the good deeds'). The -i ending is the oblique case used by feminine plurals to mark either the genitive ('… of …' / after a preposition) or the accusative (direct object); for this plural pattern the accusative and genitive share the same -i ending.
6.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound, good, upright, set right

7.meaning: A noun phrase meaning 'like the corrupters / like those who spread corruption,' i.e., those who cause ruin, disorder, and wickedness in the land. Prefixed with 'like.'
7.grammar: A masculine plural active participle ('those who corrupt') with the article al-, preceded by ka- ('like/as'). The -īna ending is the plural form used in the genitive/accusative; here the preposition ka- ('like') pulls the noun into the genitive, giving 'like the ones who corrupt.'
7.root: ف-س-د (f-s-d) — corruption, spoiling, causing ruin and disorder

8.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
8.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

9.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
9.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

10.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'or', specifically the 'or' that pairs with a preceding question to offer an alternative ('…or…?'). It links two possibilities being weighed against each other, often after an opening interrogative.

parts.en: or (in alternatives, esp. after a question)

10.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case or tense ending). It typically introduces the second branch of a two-part question or a balanced alternative, presenting the two as equally consequential.
10.root: — (particle; no triliteral root)

11.meaning: we appoint / we assign / we make — to set, render, or designate something as a particular thing or for a particular purpose.
11.grammar: A present-tense verb. The na- prefix means 'we' (the doer), and the final -u marks the ordinary (indicative) present tense: a simple statement of doing, 'we make/appoint'.
11.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, place, render, appoint

12.meaning: The God-conscious / the mindful — those who guard themselves against wrongdoing out of reverent awareness of Allah (taqwā), shielding their souls by dutiful caution. The "al-" makes it definite ("the mindful ones").

parts.en: one who is God-conscious / guards himself

12.grammar: A definite active participle in the masculine sound plural (singular "muttaqin"). The "-īna" ending is the plural form in the genitive/accusative (oblique) case — used for governed nouns, objects, or after prepositions.

13.meaning: A noun phrase meaning 'like the wicked / like the shamelessly immoral,' referring to those who brazenly break out of obedience and plunge into sin. Prefixed with 'like.'
13.grammar: A plural noun (the fuʿʿāl pattern, an intensive plural describing habitual doers) with the article al-, preceded by ka- ('like/as'). The -i ending is genitive, here because the preposition ka- ('like') governs the following noun.
13.root: ف-ج-ر (f-j-r) — to break out into sin, act shamelessly, immorality

1.meaning: A book, scripture, or written record — that which is written. It denotes a written document, and in the religious sense a revealed Scripture sent down from Allah.
1.grammar: A noun ('a book') with the -un ending, the nominative indefinite case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence. The form names a written or revealed text without specifying which.

2.meaning: 'We sent it down / revealed it'. Past-tense verb from anzala ('to send down, cause to descend'), with the 'We' of majesty as subject and 'it' as object. Characteristically used of revelation sent down from above.

parts.en: sent down / caused to descend (causative stem)

2.grammar: A past-tense verb of the causative pattern (af ʿala: 'to make come down'). The suffix -nā marks a first-person plural subject, 'we'. The attached -hu is the object 'it/him'. In divine speech the plural 'We' conveys majesty, not number.
2.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to come down, descend; (causative) to send down

3.meaning: 'To you' (addressing one person): indicating direction or motion toward a single individual — that toward which something moves or is directed.
3.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to, towards') with an attached pronoun; before a suffix ilā takes the form ilay-. The -ka ending is the pronoun 'you' for a single male addressee. Pronouns following a preposition stand in the genitive relationship, though their form does not visibly change for case.

4.meaning: 'blessed; full of and bestowing blessing'. The passive participle of bāraka ('to bless'), describing something endowed with abundant, lasting good (baraka) and a source of it.
4.grammar: A passive participle ('blessed') on the pattern mufāʿal. The ending -un (tanwīn with -u) is the indefinite nominative: it marks the word as indefinite and as standing in the subject/predicate position, e.g. describing something as 'a blessed (thing)'.
4.root: ب-ر-ك (b-r-k) — to be/become blessed; abundant, enduring good

5.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'that they may reflect deeply / ponder and consider carefully,' i.e., examine a matter thoroughly, weighing its meanings and outcomes. The doubled middle gives the sense of careful, repeated consideration.
5.grammar: A third-person masculine plural present-tense verb prefixed with li- ('so that, in order that'). The ya- prefix with the -ū ending means 'they (males).' After li-, the verb is subjunctive and its normal ending is dropped, leaving -ū — marking purpose ('so that they may ponder').
5.root: د-ب-ر (d-b-r) — the back/end of a thing; to consider outcomes, ponder consequences

6.meaning: 'His signs / His verses.' The plural of a word meaning a sign, token, or mark that points to a greater reality — also used for the verses of revelation — here joined to 'his'.
6.grammar: A sound feminine plural ('signs') with an attached possessive 'his'. The -i ending is the genitive case, the form this plural takes when it follows a preposition or is linked as the object of a possessor; the -hi ('his') marks ownership: 'his signs'.
6.root: أ-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, token, mark; a verse of revelation

7.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'and that he may take heed / be reminded / call to mind,' i.e., recollect and pay heed to a reminder so as to act upon it.
7.grammar: A third-person masculine singular present-tense verb prefixed with wa- ('and') and li- ('so that'). The ya- prefix marks 'he.' The reflexive tV pattern (yatafaʿʿal) gives the sense of bringing something to one's own mind. The -a ending is subjunctive, the mood after li- ('so that'), marking purpose.
7.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention, call to mind, take heed

8.meaning: 'Possessors of / owners of / people of' — a plural construct word meaning those endowed with or characterized by whatever follows it (e.g. 'those of understanding'). It has no singular of its own form and is always joined to a following noun.
8.grammar: A masculine plural noun used only in the construct state (always followed by another noun, 'possessors OF ...'). The -ū ending is the nominative plural form, marking it as the subject or doer of a sentence. The trailing alif is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.
8.root: — (a word for 'possessors of', having no verbal root)

9.meaning: The kernels, cores, or innermost parts — figuratively the faculties of sound reason and understanding, the discerning intellect that grasps the heart of a matter. The prefixed "al-" makes it definite ("the").
9.grammar: A definite plural noun (singular "lubb"). The '-i' ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("… OF …") or follows a preposition. Here the genitive marks it as the thing possessed after a possessor-word.

1.meaning: 'And We bestowed / granted' — to give freely as a gift or favour, with no expectation of return, prefixed with 'and'.

parts.en: bestowed, granted as a gift (past stem)

1.grammar: A past-tense verb prefixed with 'wa' ('and'). The '-nā' ending marks the doer as 'we', giving 'and we bestowed'.
1.root: و-ه-ب (w-h-b) — to give freely, to bestow as a gift

2.meaning: A proper name meaning 'to / for Dāwūd (David),' the prophet-king David, governed by the preposition 'to/for.'
2.grammar: A proper name preceded by li- ('to/for'). The name ends in -a rather than the usual -i after a preposition because, as a foreign (non-Arabic) proper name, it is 'diptote' — it resists the normal genitive -i and takes -a in its place. So li- governs it, but it shows -a.
2.root: — (proper name)

3.meaning: Sulaymān (Solomon) — the proper name of the prophet-king Solomon, son of David.
3.grammar: A proper name. The '-a' ending is the form this name takes in the genitive/accusative; as a foreign (non-Arabic) proper name it is diptote, meaning it resists the usual case-marking and takes '-a' for cases other than the nominative, without nunation.

4.meaning: How excellent! How good! A fixed verb of praise used to declare that something is outstandingly good. It is not an ordinary action verb but a formula that lavishes commendation on whatever follows it.

parts.en: how excellent is / what a good

4.grammar: A frozen verb of praise. It does not inflect for ordinary tense; it stands at the head of a statement to commend the noun that comes after it as supremely good. The closing -a is part of its fixed form rather than a productive case ending.

5.meaning: A noun meaning 'the servant / the slave / the worshipping bondsman,' i.e., one wholly owned by and devoted to his master — in the religious sense, a human being in humble servitude before Allah. It is a title of honor when applied to a devoted worshipper.
5.grammar: A masculine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -u ending is nominative: it typically marks the noun as the subject or the thing being identified ('the servant is …').
5.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to serve, worship, be a devoted bondsman

6.meaning: An emphasis particle fused with a pronoun, meaning 'indeed He' or 'truly He'. The particle inna strongly affirms and certifies the statement that follows ('it is certainly the case that…'), with 'He' as its subject.
6.grammar: The emphasising particle inna ('indeed/truly') with the attached pronoun -hu ('He'). inna affirms and strengthens the whole statement and grammatically takes a following noun or pronoun as its subject. The lengthened -hū is how this pronoun is pronounced after an -u vowel.

7.meaning: One who turns back again and again — a person who keeps returning, repeatedly coming back to Allah in repentance and remembrance. The intensive pattern stresses habitual, oft-repeated returning rather than a single act.
7.grammar: A masculine intensive noun/adjective (the 'fa''āl' pattern denoting one who does something much or habitually) with nunation. The final -un is the nominative case with nunation: the nominative is the case of the subject or of a simple predicate ('he is …'), and the added 'n' sound marks it as indefinite.
7.root: أ-و-ب (ʾ-w-b) — to return, come back; turning back (in repentance)

1.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

2.meaning: Was shown, presented, or displayed for inspection; brought forward and set before someone to be looked over or reviewed. The passive voice reports the action without naming who performed it — something 'was paraded' or 'was put on view'.

parts.en: was displayed / was presented (passive verb; the u-i-a vowelling on the three root letters marks 'was done')

2.grammar: A past-tense verb in the passive voice, built on the فُعِلَ pattern (ʿu-ri-ḍa): the internal vowels u-i signal 'was/were done' without naming the doer. It is a third-person masculine singular ('he/it') form, which in the past tense carries NO separate subject suffix — it is the bare stem, and the final -a is simply part of the passive vowel pattern, not a personal ending. Past tense reports a completed event.
2.root: ع-ر-ض (ʿ-r-ḍ) — to present, display, show, set before

3.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
3.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

4.meaning: In the evening / late afternoon — the part of the day from after midday or mid-afternoon until nightfall.
4.grammar: The noun 'evening' with the definite article al- and the preposition bi- ('in/at'). The final -i is the genitive ending, which is required after a preposition and marks the word as its object.
4.root: ع-ش-و / ع-ش-ي (ʿ-sh-w/y) — evening, nightfall, dimness of sight

5.meaning: Horses that stand poised on three legs while resting the tip of the fourth hoof on the ground — a mark of a spirited, well-bred steed. The word evokes thoroughbred horses standing alert and at attention.

parts.en: standing-poised ones (the feminine-plural form of the masculine active participle صَافِن, here describing horses, which are grammatically feminine)

5.grammar: A definite plural participle ('the ones that stand poised'). The base صَافِن is a masculine active participle; the -āt- here is its sound feminine plural, used because horses are treated as grammatically feminine. The final -u is the nominative case, which typically marks the word as the SUBJECT or as the thing being talked about ('the … are/were …').
5.root: ص-ف-ن (ṣ-f-n) — to stand on three legs with one hoof tipped; (of a horse) to stand poised

6.meaning: Swift, fleet, fine-running horses; coursers prized for their speed and noble breeding. A descriptive term for excellent steeds, emphasizing fast and graceful running.
6.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the swift horses'). The final -u is the nominative case, which generally marks the word as the SUBJECT of a sentence or as a noun standing in apposition to (renaming) another nominative noun.
6.root: ج-و-د (j-w-d) — to be excellent, fine, of good quality; (of a horse) to be swift and noble

1.meaning: 'Then he said / so he said' — the past-tense verb 'he said,' introduced by a connector meaning 'then / so,' marking what follows as the next or resulting step.
1.grammar: The prefix fa- means 'then / so,' linking this to what came before and often implying sequence or consequence. The verb is past-tense, third-person masculine singular ('he'); the final -a is the base vowel of the 3rd-person masculine singular past form, marking that a single masculine subject performed the action.

2.meaning: 'Indeed I / truly I' — an emphasis particle ('verily, indeed') that strongly affirms a statement, fused with the attached pronoun 'I.'
2.grammar: The particle inna asserts and emphasizes the statement that follows ('indeed, truly, it is certainly the case that…'). It governs its noun in the accusative; that governed noun (the ism of inna) is the attached pronoun -ī, 'I/me,' which functions as the subject of the inna-clause. The predicate then follows. So inna here takes 'I' as its accusative-governed subject.
2.root: — (particle + pronoun, no triliteral root)

3.meaning: I came to love, I held dear, I preferred — expressing one's affection, fondness, or favouring of something. The verb conveys directing one's heart's inclination toward a thing, here in the sense of cherishing or prizing it.

parts.en: to love / hold dear (stem of the Form IV verb 'aḥabba')
I (1st person singular subject ending, 'I did')

3.grammar: A past-tense verb in the first person: the -tu ending means 'I' performed the action, and the past tense marks it as already done ('I loved' / 'I came to prefer'). The doubled stem belongs to Form IV (أَحَبَّ), a derived pattern that typically adds causative/transitive force — directing love toward an object — rather than merely intensifying the simpler حَبَّ.

4.meaning: Love, deep affection, or fondness; the heart's strong inclination and attachment toward something. As a noun it names the very feeling or act of loving.
4.grammar: A verbal noun ('love, loving'). The final -a is the accusative case, which commonly marks the noun as the OBJECT of a verb (the thing loved or done) and is also the case a noun takes when it heads a possessive phrase ('love OF …').

5.meaning: The good — that which is beneficial, virtuous, and excellent; goodness as a quality or as desirable things.
5.grammar: The definite article 'the' attached to the noun 'good/goodness', which carries the -i (genitive) ending. Here the genitive is governed by a preceding preposition meaning 'toward', so the phrase reads 'toward the good'. The word covers both moral goodness and beneficial things in general.
5.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — good, goodness, to choose what is best

6.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

6.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

7.meaning: Remembrance, recollection, calling to mind; also mention, invocation, or the very words by which something is brought to mind and kept present.
7.grammar: A verbal noun ('remembrance, mention'). The final -i ending is the genitive case: it typically links the word to a following noun in a possessive or 'of' relationship, or marks it as the object of a preceding preposition ('from/of remembrance').
7.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, to mention, to call to mind

8.meaning: 'My Lord' — the Master, Sustainer and Nurturer, claimed in close personal relation by the speaker.
8.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord') with the attached pronoun -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending merges with the case-vowel of the noun, so a single long -ī is heard. The sense is 'the Lord who is mine'.
8.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

9.meaning: 'Until / up to the point that; so that' — a particle marking a limit or goal. It expresses the end-point reached ('until') or the purpose aimed at ('so that, in order that').
9.grammar: A particle indicating a goal or limit. When followed by a present-tense verb it places that verb in the subjunctive mood (clipping its ending to -a), conveying 'until / so that' something comes about. Ḥattā itself is invariable.

10.meaning: It (feminine) became hidden, slipped out of sight, or withdrew behind a screen; to veil oneself away and disappear from view. The reflexive form conveys something concealing itself or passing out of sight gradually.

parts.en: to hide oneself / withdraw from sight (reflexive 'tafāʿala' stem)
she/it (3rd person feminine singular subject ending)

10.grammar: A past-tense verb in the 'tafāʿala' reflexive pattern, meaning the subject does the action to itself ('hid itself away'). The final -t is the feminine singular subject suffix, marking a single 'she/it' as the doer. Past tense reports a completed event.
10.root: و-ر-ي (w-r-y) — to cover, conceal, hide from view

11.meaning: A barrier, screen, or veil that conceals one thing from another; a partition that blocks sight or access. The word names anything that comes between and hides what lies beyond.
11.grammar: A noun governed by the attached preposition bi- ('with/by/behind'). Because a preposition precedes it, the noun takes the genitive case, shown by the final -i: the -i ending is what a noun must wear after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… OF …').
11.root: ح-ج-ب (ḥ-j-b) — to screen, veil, block from sight, partition off

1.meaning: Give it back / return it (you plural) — restore the thing to the one it belongs to or send back what was given. The attached 'it' refers to a feminine thing.
1.grammar: A command (imperative) to a masculine plural 'you all'. The -ū marks the plural addressee; the attached -hā is the object 'it' (referring to something grammatically feminine).
1.root: ر-د-د (r-d-d) — to return, give back, send back
